image-to-base64-converter.formula:
output length = ceil(file bytes / 3) x 4
size overhead = (base64 length - file bytes) / file bytes x 100
Data URI: data:<mime>;base64,<base64 string>
Example: 3,000 bytes -> ceil(3000 / 3) x 4 = 4,000 characters,
overhead = (4000 - 3000) / 3000 x 100 = 33.3%.

keyFacts: Base64 turns binary image data into plain ASCII text that survives in HTML, CSS and JSON.
The encoding is reversible: decoding the string reproduces your exact image.
A data URI (data:image/png;base64,...) lets browsers render the image with no separate file.
Output is always about 33 percent larger than the original file.

image-to-base64-converter.workedExample:
Encode a 3,000-byte PNG.
1. Base64 processes 3 bytes at a time into 4 characters.
2. Groups: 3000 / 3 = 1000 groups.
3. Characters: 1000 x 4 = 4,000.
4. Overhead: (4000 - 3000) / 3000 x 100 = 33.3%.
5. With prefix: data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo... (the first bytes of any PNG encode to iVBORw0KGgo).
That is the exact math this tool applies to your file.
